subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Should detached longwork final-delivery ownership live as a new explicit owner-mode contract on the existing subagent delivery/registry path, or should the current requester-session-key and delivery-state substrates be extended without adding a public owner enum?
rationale: Current main has adjacent delivery-state and requester-key ownership primitives but not the requested owner-mode policy; choosing the permanent public API, default behavior, and owning substrate is product/API direction rather than a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: Use explicit owner modes
options.body: Add a narrow owner-mode contract to the existing subagent delivery registry and document default same-thread behavior plus bridge-back semantics.

options.title: Extend current requester-key substrate
options.body: Keep the public surface smaller by using completionOwnerKey and delivery state internally, adding only the minimum documented behavior needed to prevent duplicate full finals.

options.title: Move discussion to another canonical item
options.body: Close or supersede this only if maintainers pick a narrower canonical issue for final-delivery obligations and link this evidence there.

recommendation.title: Use explicit owner modes
recommendation.body: Add a narrow owner-mode contract to the existing subagent delivery registry and document default same-thread behavior plus bridge-back semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Jerry-Xin introduced the current completionOwnerKey/requester-routing split that is closest to the requested contract decision.
